template.name: Opening: The House and Its Secrets

assignments.text:
"That is no answer. One may hate many things
one has to do habitually. Your walk says that you
dislike it. It says, Here am I, who ought to be
guarded like a princess; but I am poor, I have no
escort of honour; yet here I walk, a whole retinue,
a body-guard to myself."
assignments.summary: Edward interprets Hester's gait as a walking contradiction—asserting independence while unconsciously proclaiming her poverty and need for protection—exposing the contradictions she refuses to acknowledge.
assignments.best_quote: Your walk says that you dislike it. It says, Here am I, who ought to be guarded like a princess; but I am poor, I have no escort of honour; yet here I walk, a whole retinue, a body-guard to myself

assignments.text:
"Yes? from—whom? an unsuccessful suitor: a
man that always has a right to be insulting," cried
Edward with a sort of laugh, "to relieve his mind. True! to be sure all these things are true. It is
quite right that a girl needs protection. Men are
stronger than she is, and they will insult her if it is
in their power, if not in one way then in another. The weak will always go to the wall.
assignments.summary: Edward justifies male cruelty toward women as a natural consequence of power disparity; the unprotected will be exploited because exploitation goes unpunished.
assignments.best_quote: The weak will always go to the wall. If there is nobody to take care of you, and nobody to punish me for it, of course I shall treat you badly. If I am not any worse than my neighbours I don't pretend to be any better

assignments.text:
She had taken it
upon herself, and for years past she had said to
herself that the boy had made her know, as she had
never known before, what happiness was. But now
here was, swinging round slowly, revealing itself to
her in glimpses, the reverse of the medal, the other
side of the picture. Was he deceiving her?
assignments.summary: Catherine faces the unwelcome possibility that Edward has been deceiving her about his meeting with Hester.
assignments.best_quote: But now here was, swinging round slowly, revealing itself to her in glimpses, the reverse of the medal, the other side of the picture

assignments.text:
Hester kept gazing through that wintry blackness,
with eyes still wide open, and her clear brows
puckered with wonder and alarm. Was it natural,
then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was
enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences,
to stand by the chief actor whatever happened,
but never to share in the initiative or have [Pg 125] 
any moral concern in the motive or the means of
what was done?
assignments.summary: Hester questions whether women's prescribed role—to sympathize and share consequences but never to understand or influence the action—is just or natural.
assignments.best_quote: Was it natural, then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences, to stand by the chief actor whatever happened, but never to share in the initiative or have any moral concern in the motive or the means of what was done?

assignments.text:
To this there was no reply, but a little pause
pregnant of meaning. The thrill of the significance
in it roused Hester altogether from her book: she
had not been reading much to begin with, and now
all her faculties were awakened. She understood no
reason for it, but she understood  it . Not so Catherine,
however, who took no notice, as so often
happens to the person chiefly concerned.
assignments.summary: After Catherine's complacent remark, a charged silence falls; Hester is jolted from her book and grasps some unspoken tension while Catherine, the subject of concern, remains completely unaware.
assignments.best_quote: She understood no reason for it, but she understood it.

assignments.text:
"Which there is not, thank God," she said heartily. And again there ensued that little pause. Was it
possible she did not observe it? No one echoed the
sentiment, no one even murmured the little nothings
with which a stillness, which has a meaning, is
generally filled up by some benevolent bystander. What did it mean? Hester asked herself. But
Catherine took no notice. All had gone so well with
her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.
assignments.summary: Catherine warmly asserts that work is not needed, but another charged silence falls; no one corroborates her sentiment, and the narrator reveals her dangerous lack of fear or suspicion.
assignments.best_quote: All had gone so well with her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.

assignments.text:
"I beg your pardon, Miss Hester," he cried, "I
was just going to tell something of your mother that
would please you. When I told her we wanted
money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds," said the old clerk with a [Pg 136] 
little laugh; "twenty pounds, when we wanted twice
as many thousands! But what did that matter?
assignments.summary: Mr. Rule tells Hester that when asked for help, her mother gave her entire savings of twenty pounds, though thousands were needed—an act of selfless devotion.
assignments.best_quote: When I told her we wanted money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds.

assignments.text:
Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure
and pain. Perhaps even she had never done justice
to her simple-hearted mother. She sat bolt upright
in her chair, listening with all her might. Catherine
Vernon seemed to retire from the principal place she
had hitherto held in the conversation, and Hester
came forward in her stead. She looked at the old
clerk steadily.
assignments.summary: Hester, moved by the revelation of her mother's sacrifice, sits upright with keen attention; Catherine withdraws from the center of conversation as Hester steps forward.
assignments.best_quote: Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure and pain.

assignments.text:
"You speak," she said, "of ladies only. Where
was my father?" holding Rule with her eye, so that
he could not escape.
assignments.summary: Hester demands to know where her father was during the crisis when her mother and cousin helped save the bank.
assignments.best_quote: You speak of ladies only. Where was my father?

assignments.text:
"I don't wish to look again. Is not that enough? I suppose it would make her very unhappy. She
would struggle, she would try to find excuses. Oh,
Captain Morgan, don't press me so! I suppose everything
would turn round and round. There would
seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to,
the skies would all whirl and the solid ground.
assignments.summary: Hester struggles to articulate the true emotional impact: everything becomes unstable and vertiginous; she is nearly overcome describing it.
assignments.best_quote: There would seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to, the skies would all whirl and the solid ground. It makes my head swim to think of it.

template.name: The Weight of Class and Capital

assignments.text:
"No," he said, "Catherine's growing an old maid.
She must look alive if she means to get a husband."
assignments.summary: John Vernon crudely suggests that Catherine, unmarried and aging, should hurry to find a husband.
assignments.best_quote: Catherine's growing an old maid. She must look alive if she means to get a husband.

assignments.text:
"Sir!" said Mrs. John Vernon, standing in a fine
attitude of displeasure by her desk, holding it open
with one hand. She looked like a picture by Sir
Thomas Lawrence, her scarf, for she wore a scarf,
hanging half off her pretty white shoulders, caught
upon one equally white arm, her ringlets waving on
her cheek. His laugh was rude, and then he was
only a clerk.
assignments.summary: Mrs. John Vernon stands in displeasure by her desk, her beauty and refinement momentarily masking her helplessness, like a Lawrence portrait of aristocratic offended dignity.
assignments.best_quote: Sir!

assignments.text:
And here it may be remarked that whereas Hester
was apt to be seized by sudden fits of shame at the
idea that perhaps, after all her thoughts on the
subject, he was not thinking of her at all, Edward
on the other hand felt no such alarm, and never
thought it even presumptuous on his part to assume
the certainty of her love for him, which, as the
reader knows, was a certainty to which she had not
herself attained.
assignments.summary: Edward assumes with simple certainty that Hester loves him, while Hester torments herself with the fear that he may not love her at all.
assignments.best_quote: whereas Hester was apt to be seized by sudden fits of shame at the idea that perhaps, after all her thoughts on the subject, he was not thinking of her at all, Edward on the other hand felt no such alarm, and never thought it even presumptuous on his part to assume the certainty of her love for him, which, as the reader knows, was a certainty to which she had not herself attained.

assignments.text:
But the most uneasy of
all was Hester, who that day, for the first time,
took upon her the most painful burden of women—the
half knowledge which is torture, which the
imagination endeavours to supplement in a thousand
unreal ways, knowing them to be unreal, and dismissing
them as quickly as they are formed—and
the bitter suspense, the sensation that at any moment
things may be happening, news coming which will
bring triumph or misery, but which you cannot foresee
or accelerate, or do anything but wait for.
assignments.summary: Hester enters a state of painful uncertainty and powerlessness, unable to know what Edward has done or will do, facing the specifically feminine burden of suspense and half-knowledge.
assignments.best_quote: the most uneasy of all was Hester, who that day, for the first time, took upon her the most painful burden of women—the half knowledge which is torture, which the imagination endeavours to supplement in a thousand unreal ways, knowing them to be unreal, and dismissing them as quickly as they are formed—and the bitter suspense, the sensation that at any moment things may be happening, news coming which will bring triumph or misery, but which you cannot foresee or accelerate, or do anything but wait for

assignments.text:
"Do you mean to say you did not know—the man
that was such a fool, that left it a ruin on Catherine's
hands? You did not know why she hated you? You are the only one in the place that does not. I
have taken the disease from him, through you; it
must run in the blood. Come, come, you drive me
into heroics too.
assignments.summary: Edward explains that John Vernon left the bank ruined for Catherine to salvage, and that this is why Catherine has hated Hester, information that was apparently common knowledge except to Hester herself.
assignments.best_quote: Do you mean to say you did not know—the man that was such a fool, that left it a ruin on Catherine's hands? You did not know why she hated you?

assignments.text:
And what in human form could have given a
more complete impersonation of the morning than
this girl, fresh, fair, and strong, with such a world of
latent possibilities in her? The cloud of last night's
perversity blew away. She met the eye of the day
with a gaze as open and as confident. Neither
Nature nor Hester had any fear.
assignments.summary: Hester becomes one with the radiant morning; her troubles dissolve and she embodies fearless youth and boundless potential.
assignments.best_quote: And what in human form could have given a more complete impersonation of the morning than this girl, fresh, fair, and strong, with such a world of latent possibilities in her? The cloud of last night's perversity blew away. She met the eye of the day with a gaze as open and as confident. Neither Nature nor Hester had any fear.

assignments.text:
The season, the weather, the
hour, the brown quiescent fields in which for the
only moment of the year no mystery of growth was
going on, but only a silent waiting for the seeds and
the spring; this day of leisure when everything was [Pg 52] 
at rest, all the surrounding circumstances united to
throw into full relief the strange centre to the
landscape—the two figures which brought a sharp
interest of life into this still-breathing atmosphere,
and waiting stagnation, and Sunday calm.
assignments.summary: In autumn's waiting fields on a day of complete rest, two men plot business—their restless energy a stark transgression against the stagnant, death-like landscape.
assignments.best_quote: The season, the weather, the hour, the brown quiescent fields in which for the only moment of the year no mystery of growth was going on, but only a silent waiting for the seeds and the spring; this day of leisure when everything was at rest, all the surrounding circumstances united to throw into full relief the strange centre to the landscape—the two figures which brought a sharp interest of life into this still-breathing atmosphere, and waiting stagnation, and Sunday calm.

assignments.text:
Her look as she sat gazing at him was so terrible
that he never forgot it. He did not understand it
then, nor did he ever after fully understand it. The
colour had gone entirely out of her face; her eyes
stared at him as out of two deep, wide caves. It
was a look of wonder, of dismay, of guilt. "Is he
wanted—so much?" she said.
assignments.summary: Hester's look of absolute terror and guilt at Harry's news remains with him; he intuits but cannot comprehend her involvement.
assignments.best_quote: Her look as she sat gazing at him was so terrible that he never forgot it. He did not understand it then, nor did he ever after fully understand it. The colour had gone entirely out of her face; her eyes stared at him as out of two deep, wide caves. It was a look of wonder, of dismay, of guilt.

assignments.text:
For this was the only description
that could be given. The conversation just recorded
occurred over again, as if it had been in a book. "With a lady!" "They left this afternoon."
"Reason to suppose that in the meantime—" And
then this talk, suspended in the air as it seemed,
came to a pause.
assignments.summary: Hester sits in the dark, reliving Harry's revelations as if they were a story she is reading, the information repeating like an echo.
assignments.best_quote: The conversation just recorded occurred over again, as if it had been in a book. 'With a lady!' 'They left this afternoon.' 'Reason to suppose that in the meantime—'

assignments.text:
And the silence resumed its sway. She laid
herself back as before—her pale head against the
dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time
afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily,
then there was no sound at all. The fire burned
cheerfully, the lamp shed its steady glow upon
Hester's book, to which after this talk she did not,
as may be supposed, pay very much attention.
assignments.summary: Catherine lays back with her pale head against dark curtains and becomes still. Hours pass as Hester reads, then a supernatural chill sweeps through the warm room as Hester realises Catherine's hands have grown cold.
assignments.best_quote: her pale head against the dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily, then there was no sound at all... A chill crept into the room like nothing Hester had ever felt before, though all was still, serenely warm and bright to outward appearance.

template.name: Edward's Reckoning: Speculation, Flight, and Return

assignments.text:
It made him angry, it made
him furious; it made him for the moment too much
a natural man, too sincere and real to be capable of
his usual self-suppression. Harry would have an
equal share with himself of the bank; they were
equal there in power and authority, and in the
profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry
should be his own master and Edward the slave of
an old woman!
assignments.summary: Edward's anguish intensifies as he realizes that despite equal status and wealth in the bank, Harry possesses freedom while Edward remains enslaved to Catherine's emotional demands.
assignments.best_quote: Harry would have an equal share with himself of the bank; they were equal there in power and authority, and in the profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry should be his own master and Edward the slave of an old woman!

assignments.text:
He indemnified
himself by plunging into the midst of the
bundle of papers which he had not chosen to
describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more
excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet
supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of [Pg 219] 
this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight
would scarcely have been more full of danger.
assignments.summary: Edward finds psychological compensation for his powerlessness in dangerous financial papers that contain more excitement than Harry's romantic freedom.
assignments.best_quote: He indemnified himself by plunging into the midst of the bundle of papers which he had not chosen to describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight would scarcely have been more full of danger.

assignments.text:
There was enough in the packet to tear the house
up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind
of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to
examine it as another man might have flown to
brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden
successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles
in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy
tale.
assignments.summary: The papers promise dazzling fantasies of sudden wealth and independence, to which Edward turns like a man seeking oblivion in drink or drugs.
assignments.best_quote: There was enough in the packet to tear the house up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to examine it as another man might have flown to brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy tale.

assignments.text:
He revenged himself on his bonds, on the
superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above
all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by
this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands,
to ruin them all.
assignments.summary: Edward projects his desire for revenge and liberation onto the papers, which offer the power to destroy Catherine and Harry simultaneously.
assignments.best_quote: He revenged himself on his bonds, on the superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands, to ruin them all.

template.name: Loneliness and Authority: Catherine Vernon's Paradox

assignments.text:
"Oh, Hester, it would be easy, very easy, to cease to
be unfortunate—if you choose, dear. All that part
of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you
choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence
and thinking of what Catherine will say
and what people will think. The White House—might
be yours if you liked, everything might be
yours. You would only have to say the word."
assignments.summary: Mrs. John passionately describes the transformation marriage to Harry would bring: freedom from poverty, dependence, and Catherine's control, and the restoration of the White House.
assignments.best_quote: All that part of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence and thinking of what Catherine will say and what people will think. The White House—might be yours if you liked, everything might be yours.

assignments.text:
She could put back her mother in
the White House she loved, take down the innocent
portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of
honour once more; throw open finer rooms than
Catherine's for the reception of, oh! so different a
company—society in which no one should be overlooked,
and in which Catherine's gentle rival should
be supreme. She could do all this if she chose. The
thought suddenly bursting upon her made her head
go round.
assignments.summary: Hester envisions reversing her mother's exile from the White House and making herself a rival power centre to Catherine.
assignments.best_quote: She could put back her mother in the White House she loved, take down the innocent portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of honour once more

assignments.text:
It gave her a sort of pang of amusement when she
concluded upon this—Hester! that proud, troublesome
creature—she who would never give in, who
put on the airs of a princess in the Grange drawing-room,
and declined to go to supper—she with the
spirit of a revolutionary, and the temper of a—demon—(no,
no, this was perhaps too bad—the
temper of a—Vernon, Catherine said to herself with
a laugh)—she to fall to the lot of Harry!
assignments.summary: Catherine finds the idea of Hester marrying Harry absurdly amusing—a paradoxical pairing of the ambitious, spirited girl with the placid, athletic young man.
assignments.best_quote: She to fall to the lot of Harry! This was so strangely funny, so paradoxical, so out of character, that it amused Catherine altogether beyond description, yet gave her a strange blow.

assignments.text:
This curious
pleasurable encounter, as through a veil, of two fresh
souls, hitherto unknown to each other—a moment as
full of enchantment as can be in this world—was
suddenly broken in upon by the old captain, who
jumped up, notwithstanding his rheumatism, as
quickly as a boy, and, coming between, stood up
with his back to the fire, interrupting the light.
assignments.summary: Captain Morgan suddenly jumps up and physically positions himself between Hester and Roland, breaking their nascent connection.
assignments.best_quote: This curious pleasurable encounter, as through a veil, of two fresh souls, hitherto unknown to each other—a moment as full of enchantment as can be in this world—was suddenly broken in upon

assignments.text:
In the latter
point of view, of course, no succour could have been
had from Hester; and it was the impossibility of this [Pg 120] 
which made Miss Vernon laugh. But Hester thought
it was her readiness, her devotion, her power of doing
everything that mortal woman had ever done before
her, which was doubted, and the sense that she was
neither believed in nor understood swept in a wave
of bitterness through her heart.
assignments.summary: Hester interprets Catherine's laugh as doubt in her capabilities rather than doubt about money, and this misunderstanding fills her with bitter resentment.
assignments.best_quote: Hester thought it was her readiness, her devotion, her power of doing everything that mortal woman had ever done before her, which was doubted, and the sense that she was neither believed in nor understood swept in a wave of bitterness through her heart.

assignments.text:
She
was intended to laugh, indeed, if they did not secure
another sentiment; but the first aim, and perhaps
the last aim, of the insidious Roland, had been to [Pg 79] 
secure this other sentiment. Hester did not enter
into these distinctions, but she felt them; and when
she thus put forward Mrs. Morgan's failing sight, it
was with a natural casuistry which she knew would
be partially seen through, and yet would have its
effect.
assignments.summary: The narrator explains that Roland's true aim beneath the humor was to secure genuine romantic sentiment, and that Hester deployed conscious casuistry in her defense, knowing it would be partially transparent yet effective.
assignments.best_quote: She was intended to laugh, indeed, if they did not secure another sentiment; but the first aim, and perhaps the last aim, of the insidious Roland, had been to secure this other sentiment. Hester did not enter into these distinctions, but she felt them; and when she thus put forward Mrs. Morgan's failing sight, it was with a natural casuistry which she knew would be partially seen through, and yet would have its effect.

assignments.text:
It seemed to
Hester that never in her life had she so understood
the power of fate, the moment when Nature and life
seem to stand still before some event. A minute
after, the footman came up and handed a telegram to
Edward. He tore it open with trembling hands. The
next moment he jumped up from his seat with a
suppressed cry of triumph.
assignments.summary: A telegram arrives for Edward; he opens it with trembling hands and reacts with suppressed triumph, suggesting a business crisis has been resolved favorably.
assignments.best_quote: It seemed to Hester that never in her life had she so understood the power of fate, the moment when Nature and life seem to stand still before some event.

assignments.text:
But when that vagrant sentiment comes in which is
called love (the fools! as if the appropriation of the
name to one kind of affection, and that the most
selfish of all, was not a scorn to love, the real, the
all-enduring!) what was previous virtue, what was
truth, and gratitude, and everything else in life, in
comparison? Of course they must all give place to
the fascination of a pair of shining eyes.
assignments.summary: Oliphant critiques romantic love as a selfish impulse that overrides virtue, truth, gratitude, and family bonds, mocking its supremacy.
assignments.best_quote: when that vagrant sentiment comes in which is called love (the fools! as if the appropriation of the name to one kind of affection, and that the most selfish of all, was not a scorn to love, the real, the all-enduring!)
